messages:
Jamie Park: Running into a weird one — our async python client to a Private deployment fails with certificate verify errors when hitting through an HTTP CONNECT proxy + custom CA. curl with --proxy and --cacert succeeds, but async client throws ssl.SSLCertVerificationError.

Priya Nair: can you paste the minimal repro and the exception? also which client version?

Jamie Park: repro:
```
# in container
export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/pki/ci/private-ca.pem
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:3128
python app.py
```
app.py:
```
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(base_url="https://redwood-private:8443", proxy="http://proxy.corp:3128")
await client.chat.generate(...)
```
Traceback: ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain

Eli Thompson: two common issues here: (1) aiohttp (used by async client) does not read REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE like requests does; you need to pass an SSLContext to the TCPConnector or set trust_env and let it pick up envs — but the semantics are subtle. (2) our base_url normalization used to strip explicit ports when we canonicalized URLs; if you omit :8443 the proxy/host routing can break. did you try with the exact port in the final request?

Jamie Park: i have the port in base_url, but i noticed the SDK was appending a trailing slash and the proxy returned 404 for health endpoint once. not sure if related.

Priya Nair: safe fix for users: construct ssl.SSLContext pointing at your CA bundle and pass it to AsyncClient so aiohttp verifies correctly. Example we can add to docs:
```
import ssl
from redwood import AsyncClient
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile="/etc/pki/ci/private-ca.pem")
client = AsyncClient(base_url="https://redwood-private:8443", proxy="http://proxy.corp:3128", ssl_context=ctx, trust_env=True)
```
Note: trust_env=True ensures aiohttp honors HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY in some setups.

Eli Thompson: agreed. follow-ups: (A) SDK should accept ca_bundle path string (for parity with sync client) and/or an SSLContext object; (B) doc quickstart must show proxy+private-ca troubleshooting; (C) ensure AsyncClient default for trust_env matches sync client.

Jamie Park: also a UX bug: when SSL verification fails today the error message is just "certificate verify failed" with no hint about proxies or private CAs. customers end up disabling verification. we should include a hint like "If you are using a private CA or corporate proxy, set ca_bundle or ssl_context (see redwood.dev/sdk/ssl)."

Priya Nair: good point. i'll add a short troubleshooting blurb and example to the Private deployment section. we should also mention env vars: REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and SSL_CERT_FILE affect requests but not aiohttp; for async use ssl_context or ca_bundle param.

Eli Thompson: i'll open a bug: add ca_bundle: Optional[str] and ssl_context: Optional[ssl.SSLContext] to AsyncClient __init__, wire through aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ssl_context) and honor trust_env. also add test that runs an internal proxy fixture + custom CA to avoid regressions.

docs-bot: created issue #3582: "py-async: proxy + private CA parity (ca_bundle/ssl_context) + trust_env default alignment + clearer SSL error" assigned to @Eli. PR template linked.

Jamie Park: thanks — holding off on hacky verify=False. will test the new param when available. also noted the trailing slash/port canonicalization and will attach HTTP dumps if needed.

Priya Nair: thanks everyone. i'll draft the doc snippet and drop it in the PR for review.

Eli Thompson: will update typing stubs so mypy shows the new kwargs. plan to land before next patch release.
